examples.ko: 이 단어의 원뜻은 지금 쓰는 뜻과 많이 달라요.
examples.en: The original meaning of this word is very different from how it is used now.
It's easier to understand if you look up the original meaning in a dictionary.

examples.ko: 말이 변해서 원뜻이 잊힌 표현이 많아요.
examples.en: There are many expressions whose original meaning has been forgotten as the language changed.

examples.ko: 원뜻 그대로 쓰는 사람은 요즘 별로 없어요.
examples.en: Few people use it in its original sense these days.

examples.ko: 그 속담의 원뜻이 뭔지 정말 궁금해요.
examples.en: I'm really curious what the original meaning of that proverb is.

examples.ko: 원뜻에서 조금 벗어나서 다른 뜻으로 쓰여요.
examples.en: It has drifted a bit from the original meaning and is used in another sense.

explain: 말이 시간이 지나며 바뀌었을 때, 처음 뜻과 지금 뜻을 비교하며 써요. 대화에서는 '원래 뜻', '본래 뜻'이라고도 많이 해요. 반대로 달라진 뜻은 '바뀐 뜻'이나 '비유적인 뜻'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: If you know the original meaning, the word becomes easier.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대화에서 '원뜻'보다 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: More common in conversation than 원뜻.

phrases.en: The original meaning and the current meaning are different.
phrases.nuance_ko: '원래 뜻'과 비슷하지만 조금 더 글에 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 원래 뜻 but fits writing a bit better.

phrases.en: I look up the original meaning of words I don't know.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사전이나 자료로 처음 뜻을 확인할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when checking the first meaning in a dictionary or source.
phrases.en_equiv: to look up the original meaning

explain_en: It is used when comparing a word's first meaning with its meaning now after the language has changed. In conversation people also say '원래 뜻' or '본래 뜻'. The changed meaning is called '바뀐 뜻' or '비유적인 뜻' (figurative meaning).

examples.ko: 화가인 삼촌은 집 근처에 작업실이 있어요.
examples.en: My uncle, a painter, has a studio near his house.
I painted in the studio until late at night.

examples.ko: 친구들과 함께 작업실을 빌려서 쓰고 있어요.
examples.en: I am renting and sharing a studio with friends.
The studio is quiet, so I can concentrate well.

examples.ko: 이번 주말에 새 작업실로 이사할 거예요.
examples.en: I will move to a new studio this weekend.
I bought coffee on the way to the studio.

explain: 그림, 음악, 공예처럼 무언가를 만드는 일을 하는 방에 써요. 회사에서 일하는 곳은 '사무실'이라고 해서 서로 달라요.

phrases.en: I rented a studio with my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일할 방을 따로 구할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when getting a separate room to work in.

phrases.en: I go to my studio every weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작업하는 방으로 간다는 뜻의 가장 기본적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic way to say you go to your workroom.

phrases.en: I work in a small studio.
phrases.nuance_ko: '사무실에서 일하다'와 달리 만드는 일을 하는 곳을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Unlike working in an office, this means working where you make things.

explain_en: It is used for a room where you make things, such as art, music, or crafts. A place where you work at a company is called 사무실 instead.

examples.en: The online mall has a lot of categories.
Please choose a category first.
Which category is this book in?
It's easier if you organize things by category.
The categories are in the top menu.
I tried dividing the items into categories.

explain: 온라인 쇼핑이나 앱에서 많이 써요. 일반 대화에서는 '종류'나 '분류'가 더 쉬운 말이에요. '분야'는 일이나 공부의 영역을 말할 때 써요.

phrases.en: They show the clothes divided by category.
phrases.nuance_ko: '카테고리'에 '-별로'를 붙여 종류마다 나눌 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-별로' to 카테고리 means 'by category' when sorting things into groups.

phrases.en: I organized the books by dividing them into categories.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이나 정보를 종류별로 가를 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for splitting items or information into types.

phrases.en: This item is in a different category.
phrases.nuance_ko: '다른'을 앞에 붙여 같은 종류가 아닌 곳을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Putting '다른' before it points to a different group from the current one.

explain_en: It is common in online shopping and apps. In general conversation '종류' or '분류' are easier words. '분야' is used for a field of work or study.

en: to indicate; to mark; to display

examples.ko: 지도에 가고 싶은 곳을 표시해 보세요.
examples.en: Try marking the places you want to go on the map.
I marked the important parts of the textbook in yellow.

examples.ko: 달력에 시험 날짜를 별 모양으로 표시해요.
examples.en: I mark the exam date on the calendar with a star.
Many shops display their prices in large print.
Mark your answer with a circle.

examples.ko: 저는 빨간 펜으로 표시하는 습관이 있어요.
examples.en: I have a habit of marking things with a red pen.

explain: '표시하다'는 나중에 쉽게 찾으려고 눈에 띄게 해 두는 일에 써요. 말할 때는 '체크하다'도 많이 쓰고, 글자 아래에 줄을 그으면 '밑줄을 치다', 동그라미를 그리면 '동그라미를 치다'라고 해요. 가격표나 화면처럼 눈에 보이게 나타난 건 '표시되다'로 말해요.

phrases.en: I check off the important dates on the calendar.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 '표시하다' 대신 많이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common spoken alternative to '표시하다'.

phrases.en: Please circle the answer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동그라미를 그려서 눈에 띄게 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you draw a circle to make something stand out.

phrases.en: I underlined the words I didn't know.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글자 아래에 줄을 그어 표시할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you mark text by drawing a line under it.

explain_en: '표시하다' is for making something stand out so you can find it later. In casual talk people also say '체크하다' (check off); drawing a line under words is '밑줄을 치다' and drawing a circle is '동그라미를 치다'. Things that simply show up, like a price tag or something on a screen, use the passive '표시되다'.

examples.en: On busy mornings I simply get by with bread.

examples.ko: 이 앱으로 간편히 송금할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can send money easily with this app.
I packed light and left for the trip.
Please come dressed casually.

examples.ko: 간편히 먹을 수 있는 도시락을 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a lunch box that is easy to eat.
Is there a convenient way to submit the documents?

explain: '간편하게'와 같은 뜻이에요. 말할 때는 '간편하게'를 쓰기도 하고, '간편히'는 안내문이나 광고 문구에서도 볼 수 있어요. 형용사는 '간편하다'예요.

phrases.en: It's food you can eat easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: '간편히'와 뜻이 같고 말할 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 간편히 and more common in speech.

phrases.en: I came in simple, comfortable clothes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 형용사 '간편하다'를 명사 앞에 붙이는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective 간편하다 placed before a noun.

phrases.en: This bag is light and convenient.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문장을 끝낼 때 쓰는 해요체예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Polite form used to end a sentence.

explain_en: It means the same as '간편하게'. In speech people also say '간편하게', and '간편히' can be seen in notices and ads. The adjective is '간편하다'.

examples.en: The apartment security guard said hello.
I left the parcel with the security guard.

examples.ko: 밤에는 경비원 두 명이 건물을 지켜요.
examples.en: At night, two guards watch over the building.
The guard came to work early in the morning.

examples.ko: 저는 경비원을 불러서 문을 열어 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: I called the guard and asked him to open the door.
The bank's guard is kind to customers too.

explain: 아파트에서는 친근하게 '경비 아저씨'라고도 불러요. '-원'은 일하는 사람을 뜻해서 은행원, 회사원, 공무원처럼 다른 직업 이름에도 붙어요.

phrases.en: I said hello to the security guard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아파트에서 친근하게 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A friendly way to address the guard at an apartment complex.

phrases.en: The apartment security guard opened the door for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일하는 장소를 앞에 붙여서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The workplace is put in front to be specific.

phrases.en: If there's a problem, tell the security guard.
phrases.nuance_ko: '에게'를 붙여 도움이나 연락을 청할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '에게', used when asking the guard for help.

explain_en: In apartment buildings, people also call them 경비 아저씨 in a friendly way. The ending -원 means a worker, and it appears in job names such as 은행원, 회사원, and 공무원.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날에 과속하면 아주 위험해요.
examples.en: Speeding on a rainy day is very dangerous.

examples.ko: 아버지는 운전할 때 절대 과속하지 않으세요.
examples.en: My father never speeds when he drives.
The car was speeding and got caught by the police.
Yesterday I saw a speeding car on the highway.
I almost had an accident because I was speeding.
I was worried my friend might speed.

explain: 도로의 제한 속도를 넘어 달릴 때 써요. 명사 '과속'에 다른 말을 붙여 '과속 운전', '과속 단속'처럼도 말해요.

phrases.en: Speeding is a cause of accidents.
phrases.nuance_ko: 제한 속도보다 빨리 운전하는 일을 명사로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun phrase for driving faster than the speed limit.

phrases.example: 이 길에는 과속 단속 카메라가 있어요.
phrases.en: There is a speed enforcement camera on this road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과속하는 차를 잡는 일이에요. 경찰이나 도로 안내에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Catching speeding cars; common in police and road notices.

phrases.en: It's raining, so please don't speed.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 마세요'는 하지 말라고 부드럽게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-지 마세요' politely tells someone not to do something.

explain_en: Use it when driving over the speed limit. The noun '과속' also combines with other words, as in '과속 운전' and '과속 단속'.

examples.en: It is hard to tell the twins apart.
Can you tell real from fake?
The colors were so similar that I couldn't tell them apart.

examples.ko: 공과 사를 구별하는 사람이 좋은 직원이에요.
examples.en: A person who separates work from private matters is a good employee.
I want to distinguish the pronunciation of the two words.

examples.ko: 아이들은 아직 꿈과 현실을 구별하지 못해요.
examples.en: Children can't yet tell dreams from reality.

explain: 구별하다는 둘 이상이 서로 다르다는 것을 알아보고 나누는 거예요. '구분하다'와 거의 같게 쓰는데, 구분하다는 기준에 따라 나눈다는 느낌이 더 강하고 구별하다는 차이를 알아본다는 느낌이 더 강해요. 보통 'A와 B를 구별하다'로 써요.

phrases.example: 두 소리가 비슷해서 구별이 안 돼요.
phrases.en: The two sounds are similar, so I can't tell them apart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차이를 모르겠다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you can't see the difference.

phrases.example: 저는 두 색을 구별할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: I can tell the two colors apart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 능력이 있다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you are able to do it.

phrases.en: I tell apples and pears apart by taste.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 가지를 비교할 때 쓰는 기본 틀이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic pattern for comparing two things.

explain_en: 구별하다 is to recognize that two or more things differ and tell them apart. It is close to '구분하다', which leans more toward dividing things by a standard, while 구별하다 leans toward noticing the difference. The usual pattern is 'A와 B를 구별하다'.

examples.en: I was so glad to see my friend after a long time.
In my delight, I shouted without realizing it.
He couldn't hide his delight and smiled.
I felt surprise before I felt gladness.
I was half glad and half worried.

examples.ko: 오래된 편지를 읽고 반가움과 그리움을 느꼈어요.
examples.en: Reading the old letter, I felt gladness and longing.

explain: '반갑다'에서 나온 말로, 만나거나 소식을 들었을 때의 기쁜 마음을 말해요. 그냥 '기쁨'보다 사람이나 소식과 연결된 느낌이에요. 직접 인사할 때는 명사보다 '반가워요'를 써요.

phrases.en: I felt joy when I heard my friend's voice.
phrases.nuance_ko: '반가움'이라는 마음을 직접 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to name the feeling of gladness directly.

phrases.en: I heard some welcome news today.
phrases.nuance_ko: '반갑다'의 활용형으로, 기쁜 소식을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form of 반갑다 used for happy news.

phrases.en: I'm really glad to see you after so long.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인사할 때는 명사 대신 이 말을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this instead of the noun when greeting someone.

explain_en: It comes from '반갑다' and describes the happy feeling on meeting someone or hearing news. Compared with plain '기쁨', it is tied to a person or news. When greeting someone directly, say '반가워요' rather than this noun.

examples.ko: 가전제품을 사면 보증서를 꼭 받아 두세요.
examples.en: When you buy an appliance, be sure to get the warranty.
Without the warranty, it's hard to get free repairs.
The date of purchase is written on the warranty.

examples.ko: 시계가 고장 나서 보증서를 들고 서비스센터에 갔어요.
examples.en: My watch broke, so I took the warranty to the service center.
I lost the warranty. Would the receipt work?

examples.ko: 이 보증서는 일 년 동안만 효력이 있어요.
examples.en: This warranty is valid for only one year.

explain: 물건을 산 뒤 일정 기간 무료로 고쳐 준다고 약속하는 문서예요. 수리를 받는 것은 'A/S'(에이에스)라고 많이 말해요. 영수증과 함께 보관하라고 하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: I keep the warranty together with the receipt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나중에 수리받을 때 필요해서 잘 둔다고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for keeping it safe because you need it for repairs later.

phrases.en: The warranty period is one year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무료로 고쳐 주는 기간을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The period during which repairs are free.

phrases.example: 보증서가 있으면 A/S를 무료로 받을 수 있어요.
phrases.en: With the warranty, you can get repair service for free.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 산 뒤 수리나 점검을 받는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to getting repair or check-up service after buying a product.

explain_en: It is a document promising free repairs for a set period after you buy something. Getting repairs is often called 'A/S' (after-sales service). People often tell you to keep it together with the receipt.

en: precaution against fire; watching out for fire

examples.en: Being careful with fire is even more important in dry weather.

examples.ko: 겨울이 되면 학교에서 불조심 포스터를 그려요.
examples.en: When winter comes, we draw fire-safety posters at school.

examples.ko: 불조심 기간에 소방서에서 안전 교육을 해요.
examples.en: During fire-safety week the fire station gives safety training.

examples.ko: 집을 비울 때는 불조심을 꼭 하세요.
examples.en: Be sure to be careful with fire when you leave the house.

examples.ko: 산에 갈 때는 불조심에 신경 써야 해요.
examples.en: When you go to the mountains, you have to pay attention to fire safety.
There are signs saying 'Watch out for fire' all over the place.

explain: '불조심하세요'처럼 인사나 주의 말로도 많이 써요. 포스터나 표지판에서는 '꺼진 불도 다시 보자' 같은 표어와 함께 자주 볼 수 있어요. 더 딱딱한 말로는 '화재 예방'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The weather is dry, so be careful with fire.
phrases.nuance_ko: '불조심'을 동사처럼 써서 주의를 줄 때 하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses 불조심 like a verb to give a warning or a reminder.

phrases.en: We made fire-safety slogans at school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불조심을 알리는 짧은 문구를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the short slogans that promote fire safety.

phrases.en: The fire station gives fire prevention education.
phrases.nuance_ko: '불조심'보다 딱딱한 말로, 뉴스나 안내문에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more formal term than 불조심, common in news and notices.

explain_en: It is also used as a warning, as in '불조심하세요'. On posters and signs you often see it with slogans like '꺼진 불도 다시 보자' (check even a put-out fire again). A more formal expression is '화재 예방' (fire prevention).

en: to quicken; to hasten; to accelerate

examples.en: Please do the homework a bit faster.

examples.ko: 저는 일을 빨리해야 퇴근할 수 있어요.
examples.en: I can leave work only if I get things done quickly.

examples.ko: 준비를 빨리하면 일찍 출발할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you get ready quickly, we can leave early.
I did the dishes quickly and then rested.
I'm trying to make decisions quickly.
I tend to wash my face quickly in the morning.

explain: '일을 빨리하다'처럼 동작을 서두를 때 써요. '빨리 하다'로 띄어 쓰기도 해요. 말할 때는 '빨리 가다', '빨리 먹다'처럼 부사 '빨리'를 다른 동사 앞에 붙이는 일이 더 많고, 재촉할 때는 '빨리빨리', '서둘러 주세요'를 자주 써요.

phrases.en: Please do this work a little faster.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대에게 서둘러 달라고 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask someone to hurry.

phrases.example: 너무 빨리하지 마세요. 실수할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Don't do it too fast. You might make mistakes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 천천히 하라고 말릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to tell someone to slow down.

phrases.en: Try doing it a little faster.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부드럽게 권하는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A gentle way of encouraging someone to speed up.

explain_en: Used when you hurry an action, like doing a task quickly. It can also be written with a space: '빨리 하다'. In speech, people more often put the adverb 빨리 before another verb, as in '빨리 가다' and '빨리 먹다'. To urge someone, '빨리빨리' and '서둘러 주세요' are very common.
